title: Is Your AI Medical Interpreter HIPAA Compliant? August 2026 Guide
summary: Review an AI medical interpreter for HIPAA workflows using a practical checklist for BAAs, PHI data flows, safeguards, devices, and integrations.
body_markdown:
###


No. HHS does not give vendors a general HIPAA certification. A healthcare organization should review the exact service, contract, safeguards, configuration, and workflow it plans to use.


###


A BAA is generally needed when the vendor is acting as a business associate by handling protected health information on behalf of a covered entity. Confirm the relationship with privacy and legal counsel and make sure the exact product is covered.


###


No. Encryption is one safeguard. The review also covers risk analysis, access, devices, workforce practices, logging, incident response, contracts, retention, and other administrative, physical, and technical safeguards.


###


Yes. HIPAA addresses protected health information, not clinical interpretation accuracy. Review language-specific evidence, error handling, and safety controls separately.


###


Test sign-in and sign-out, shared devices, phone and telehealth workflows, EHR data flow, retention, logs, incident reporting, downtime, escalation, and the clinical performance of the languages in scope.
